channel.title: The Wang Report · Geopolitical
channel.description: The Wang Report Geopolitical desk: daily briefings and weekly columns.

item.title: Beijing vows South China Sea measures as Manila protests war remarks
item.description: A summons puts the dispute before China's ambassador while the practical consequences remain with the people operating at sea.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Taiwan Detains Two Drone Executives Over Chinese Chips in Military Contracts
item.description: The detentions put suppliers under scrutiny, with the consequences for contracted equipment still unestablished.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Taiwan counts seven Chinese official ships whose role the tally leaves open
item.description: A daily defence tally shows the assessment that proposed satellite analysis must help Taiwan make.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Philippines protests Chinese envoy's threat of force over disputed waters
item.description: Beijing's claim to decide where Philippine vessels belong puts the consequences of a diplomatic threat aboard the next ship it challenges.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Taiwan unveils 500-kilometre attack drone with fielding still the test
item.description: The weapon’s military value turns on whether Taiwanese crews can field it while China gathers information about their approaches.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The HKMA Tells Banks To Lend The Yuan
item.description: The HKMA and Beijing have solved offshore yuan supply this week, but whether Bank of China, HSBC and Standard Chartered actually lend it abroad is a harder problem policy cannot solve.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Trump Banks Taiwan's Interceptors For Two More Summits
item.description: Xi Jinping pressed Trump this week to halt Taiwan arms sales under a decades-old communique, and Trump left a $14 billion interceptor package undecided, again, pushing the answer onto two more summits.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The Rate Hike That Missed Hong Kong's Mortgages
item.description: The HKMA raised its Base Rate to track the Fed, but a wall of mainland liquidity had already set Hong Kong's real borrowing cost 138 basis points lower.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Trump Calls Taiwan's Weapons 'Chips To Play'
item.description: Trump's own description of Taiwan's arms shipments as bargaining chips is the real Taiwan policy this week, not whatever he and Xi say for cameras on September 24.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The Pension Fund That Skips The Quota Line
item.description: China's state pension fund is drafting a quota-free route into Hong Kong's bond market as Beijing shuts the retail channel ordinary mainlanders used to move money out.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Beijing Prices Trump's Summit At $14 Billion
item.description: China's threat to cancel Xi's September 24 White House visit over a $14 billion Taiwan arms sale turns Taipei's procurement calendar into Washington's summit currency.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Beijing Sends The Cigarette Maker To The Bank
item.description: China's finance ministry funded a 360 billion yuan bank and insurer rescue partly through the state tobacco monopoly, and investors read the choice as a warning, not a fix.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: HSBC's Deadline Lands On Mainland Money
item.description: HSBC's app-based fund-source deadline this week is the retail edge of a capital-account clampdown that is widening Hong Kong's institutional pipes while narrowing its retail ones.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Xi's Military Command Down To Two
item.description: Beijing dismissed its second-highest military officer this week, leaving Xi Jinping's command body with two members before his 2027 deadline, and the field record argues against reading it as retreat.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The CSRC Runs Hong Kong's IPO Clock
item.description: HKEX's twelve-month waiver eases the paperwork on Hong Kong's 500-company IPO backlog but leaves untouched the CSRC's pre-approval gate that actually sets the pace.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Taiwan Buys The Jets, Not The Drones
item.description: Taiwan's record NT$1.12 trillion defense budget grows the conventional hardware line the legislature spared in May and leaves untouched the asymmetric drone fleet it gutted.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Deutsche Bank Gets Beijing's Frankfurt Mandate
item.description: Beijing's decision to let Deutsche Bank clear renminbi in Frankfurt builds offshore settlement capacity that bypasses Hong Kong, and the signal matters more in years than in this one designation.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Taiwan's Budget Fight Was Never About the NT$63.4 Billion
item.description: Taiwan's opposition restored every dollar of contested drone funding it spent 266 days threatening to cut, proving the fiscal objection was cover for something else.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Beijing Taxes the Trust It Tracked to Hong Kong
item.description: Beijing's offshore trust tax and Hong Kong's bond futures contract are the same instrument read from opposite directions: capital Beijing can trace is welcome, capital it cannot is taxed.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Beijing's Martyrs Were Killed By Beijing
item.description: Beijing waited eleven months to admit its coast guard killed two of its own sailors chasing a Philippine boat, then invoked the deaths to justify harsher tactics ahead.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The Peg Pays For The Pipe
item.description: Hong Kong's new offshore bond futures and Beijing's widened capital channels are being financed, in part, by the same HIBOR spike squeezing the mortgages of Hong Kong homeowners.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: The Trigger Washington Won't Name
item.description: Washington's refusal to name the act that triggers its treaty guarantee is not prudence; it is the operating margin Beijing is now rehearsing for Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Southbound Bond Connect's Quiet Insurance Bailout
item.description: The July 7 package reads as yuan internationalization only until you notice insurers, not banks, got the new quota, and why that quota had to exist.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: The Sorties Beijing Chose Not To Fly
item.description: Beijing's Fujian drills read as an accelerating Taiwan crisis, but PLA sorties near the island just hit a three-year low, and the coercion moved to the Philippines instead.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: 94 Percent of Six Trillion Yuan, Four New Channels
item.description: Four channel-opening announcements this month read as RMB internationalization only until you notice they cluster exactly when Beijing's local-government debt-swap relief runs out.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Beijing's Coercion Tool Bypasses The Chip Fight
item.description: TSMC's $100 billion Arizona pledge is reviving 'silicon shield' anxiety, but Beijing's new extraterritorial law targets individual Taiwanese where chip leverage cannot reach.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: CNY800bn: The Freeze That Made The Widening Possible
item.description: Beijing's July 7 package reads as capital account liberalization only if you ignore the two-year retail brokerage freeze it completed the same week.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: The Statement Was Never For Beijing
item.description: The joint statement rejecting China's maritime claims was addressed to Beijing in form only; its real target is a Code of Conduct that Manila's own chairmanship cannot deliver.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: The Anniversary Statement Changed Nothing at Sea
item.description: The rejection of a decade-old ruling is not this week's real story; a stalling Code of Conduct and Iran's pull on the Pacific fleet are.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Beijing Widens the Hong Kong Pipe, Not the Door
item.description: The Hong Kong package expands how much capital can move through state-monitored channels, while a new outbound investment law narrows every channel outside them. That pairing is the actual policy.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Beijing's SLBM Test Radicalizes Fiji, Not Taipei
item.description: Beijing built the July 6 submarine missile test to punish Canberra's new Pacific pact, but the coercion that wears Taipei down is radicalizing the smaller states it also hit.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: CSRC's 2.2 Billion Yuan Fine Redirects Hong Kong Flows
item.description: The crackdown on informal cross-border brokerages does not shrink Hong Kong's role as capital gateway. It narrows the paths money can take to get there, and that narrowing is the point.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Taiwan's $25 Billion Answer to a Frozen $14 Billion
item.description: The $14 billion arms freeze and Taiwan's collapsing conscript pool arrived in the same month, and Taipei's answer to both was to stop treating Washington as the plan.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: HKEX's August 3 Futures and the Futu Shutdown
item.description: Beijing is not closing its capital architecture, it is rebuilding it so that only state-sanctioned instruments survive the renovation.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: 52 Percent of PLA Leadership, Six Generals in One Day
item.description: Xi's removal of six generals in a single day and a completed US warship replica in Xinjiang are not separate stories; together they define whether Beijing's military is hardening or fracturing.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen
